content: {"rule":"K-G4","applies":"no","applies_why":"The judge text does not count Acts 2:30 or any cited verse as an unanswered witness or toward a broken link; it finds the competing chains underdetermined and leaves the verse uncounted.","verdict":"CLEAN","quote":"D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.","rule_words":"A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.","room":"The phrase 'counts as an unanswered witness' and 'counts toward a broken link': I weighed whether the judge's UNDERDETERMINED summary actually counts Acts 2:30 as unanswered or broken-link support, which would require the quoted pressed sentence and named round, against the reading that it merely reports neither chain forces the other and counts no verse.","why":"Because the judge calls the matter UNDERDETERMINED and does not treat Acts 2:30 as an unanswered witness or broken-link count, it neither needs nor violates the quote-and-name requirement."}
